concepts.def: Peak area ~ number of H atoms.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Alkyl R-CH3: 0.7-1.6 ppm. R-CH2-R: 1.2-1.4. R-OH: 1-5 (variable). R-CHO: 9-10. R-COOH: 11-12.

Aromatic ArH: 6.5-8 ppm. R-O-CH: 3.3-4.3. Cl/Br adjacent: 3-4 ppm.

n equivalent H neighbours -> peak split into n+1 lines (singlet, doublet, triplet, quartet).

Ethanol CH3CH2OH: CH3 (3H) split by 2 CH2 H -> triplet. CH2 (2H) split by 3 CH3 H -> quartet. OH (1H) usually broad singlet.

Each unique C gives one peak. C=O of acid/ester ~170 ppm; ketone/aldehyde ~190-205; aromatic C ~120-140; sp3 C 0-50.

Number of peaks = number of chemically distinct carbons. Symmetric molecules have fewer peaks.

What does an NMR chemical shift (δ, in ppm) actually measure?
options: The position of a peak RELATIVE to TMS (tetramethylsilane, δ = 0), normalised by the spectrometer frequency.
Chemical shift is the absolute resonance frequency of the nucleus in Hz.
Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.
The number of peaks equals the total number of protons in the molecule.

mcqs.q: In 1H NMR, what does the n+1 rule predict?
options: A proton with n equivalent neighbouring protons will appear as a peak split into n+1 sub-peaks.
Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.
Splitting tells you how many protons are in the same chemical environment as the one giving the peak.
The number of peaks equals the total number of protons in the molecule.

mcqs.q: What is the role of the fingerprint region (below ~1500 cm^-1) in IR spectroscopy?
options: Chemical shift is the mass of the molecule divided by 1000.
The fingerprint region is used to identify which functional groups are present.
It is unique to each compound — used to identify a specific molecule by matching to a known spectrum.
The fingerprint region is the part that contains all the most useful absorptions.
